summary: Defines an IKEv2 extension that lets an overloaded or maintenance-bound VPN gateway tell a client to connect to a different gateway. It lets operators spread load or take a server out of service. It is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: If one cashier has a huge line, a helper can point people to another open register. This lets a busy VPN server tell a visitor to go to a different server instead.

questions: how to redirect ikev2 clients to another gateway
how does a vpn gateway redirect a client
how to prevent ikev2 redirect loops
subtitle: How an overloaded or retiring VPN gateway can tell an IKEv2 client to connect to a different gateway.

tldr.problem: Configuring VPN gateway addresses on clients does not scale, and DNS does not let a gateway hand clients to another gateway based on load or maintenance.
tldr.mechanism: The client signals support with a REDIRECT_SUPPORTED notification, and the gateway replies with a REDIRECT notification naming another gateway. The client then repeats the exchange there, quoting the original gateway in REDIRECTED_FROM.
tldr.outcome: Gateways can spread load or be shut down for maintenance. The same mechanism can be used in Mobile IPv6 to redirect a mobile node to another home agent.

today: RFC 5685 is a Proposed Standard from November 2009. It is not marked as obsoleted or updated in the unit metadata.

sections.title: The Problem With Fixed Gateway Addresses
sections.content:
IKEv2 is used to set up IPsec-based VPNs. A gateway address can be configured on the client, but the RFC says this does not scale well when there are many gateways. Discovering gateways through DNS is widely used, but it is not flexible about assigning a gateway by load: the client typically tries the first address in the DNS response and only moves to the next one if setup fails.

This RFC adds a redirect mechanism so a gateway can send the client to another gateway, for example based on load. The redirect can happen during IKE_SA_INIT or IKE_AUTH, and a gateway-initiated redirect in the middle of a session is also supported. Redirects can also be for administrative or optimal-routing reasons, and the RFC does not try to list every reason.
sections.plainLanguage: A list of server addresses is like a list of shops: you go to the first one even if it is packed. Redirect lets a packed shop say, go next door instead.

sections.title: Redirect During the Initial Exchange
sections.content:
The client announces that it supports redirects by including a REDIRECT_SUPPORTED notification in its IKE_SA_INIT request. The gateway MUST keep track of which clients did and did not indicate support, and MUST NOT send a REDIRECT payload to a client that did not.

To redirect, the gateway picks another gateway (how it chooses is out of scope) and answers with an IKE_SA_INIT response containing a REDIRECT notification. It carries the new gateway's identity and the nonce data from the client's Ni payload. No IKE SA is created, and the responder SPI is zero.

The client MUST check that the nonce data matches what it sent, and silently discards the response if it does not. This guards against denial-of-service attacks where an attacker injects bogus responses. If the match succeeds, the client starts a new IKE_SA_INIT with the listed gateway, provided its Peer Authorization Database (PAD) allows it, and includes a REDIRECTED_FROM notification holding the original gateway's IP address.

The new gateway may redirect the client again. The client does not repeat REDIRECT_SUPPORTED, because REDIRECTED_FROM already tells the new gateway that the client supports redirects. The client MUST use the same PAD and Security Policy Database (SPD) entries as it would have used with the original gateway, and a redirect MUST NOT modify any PAD or SPD entry.
sections.plainLanguage: You knock on a door and say you are happy to be sent elsewhere. The person says go to number 7 and repeats your secret number so you know it is really them. You then knock at number 7 and say who sent you.

sections.title: Anycast Addresses
sections.content:
With anycast, the DNS stores one anycast address for the whole group of gateways instead of a list of unicast addresses. The client sends its IKE_SA_INIT request, with REDIRECT_SUPPORTED, to that address. It is routed to one gateway in the group, which replies from the anycast address.

If the request was sent to an anycast address, the gateway MUST include a REDIRECT payload pointing the client to a unicast address of one of the gateways. It MAY redirect the client to its own unicast address if it is not overloaded. The rest of the exchange is the same as in the initial-exchange case.
sections.plainLanguage: Everyone calls one shared phone number. Whoever picks up then gives you their own direct line to use from then on.

sections.title: Redirects Mid-Session and During IKE_AUTH
sections.content:
In an active session, the gateway sends an INFORMATIONAL message with a REDIRECT notification naming the new gateway. It MUST NOT include nonce data, since the message is protected by the IKEv2 security association. The client replies with a usually empty response, and the gateway retransmits until it gets one. The client SHOULD then delete its security associations with the old gateway using a DELETE payload. The gateway MAY delete them itself, but should allow enough time, configurable on the gateway, for the client to set up associations with the new gateway.

During IKE_AUTH, the gateway can redirect based on the client's identity. It prevents creation of a CHILD SA and puts the REDIRECT in the IKE_AUTH response. The gateway MUST verify the client's AUTH payload first, and the client MUST verify the gateway's AUTH payload before acting. The client SHOULD then delete the IKEv2 security association.

With EAP or multiple authentication methods, the gateway may redirect based on an exchange with an AAA or external authentication server, and MUST send the REDIRECT in the first or last IKE_AUTH response. The client MUST NOT accept a REDIRECT in an intermediate IKE_AUTH response. With EAP the gateway MAY also redirect based on the unauthenticated identity in the first exchange; it MUST still include its own AUTH payload.
sections.plainLanguage: A shop can send you elsewhere after you are already inside, or at the checkout once it knows who you are. Either way, you must be sure the message is really from the shop.

sections.title: The Three Notify Messages
sections.content:
All three messages are IKEv2 Notify payloads. In each, the Protocol ID MUST be 0 and the SPI Size MUST be 0, because the notification is not specific to one security association.

  • REDIRECT_SUPPORTED (16406): sent in the initial request to say the initiator supports redirect. It has no data beyond the notify header.
  • REDIRECT (16407): carries a gateway identity type, a length, the new gateway identity and, only in an IKE_SA_INIT response, nonce data. The nonce size MUST be between 16 and 256 bytes. Nonce data MUST NOT be included in an IKE_AUTH response or a gateway-initiated redirect.
  • REDIRECTED_FROM (16408): sent in the request to the new gateway, with the original gateway's address. If the first request went to an anycast address, that anycast address is included.

The gateway identity type is 1 for an IPv4 address, 2 for an IPv6 address and 3 for an FQDN. In REDIRECTED_FROM only types 1 and 2 are valid.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three little notes: one says I can be sent elsewhere, one says go here, and one says I was sent by that other shop.

sections.title: Loops, Mobile IPv6 and Other Peers
sections.content:
A client could be redirected repeatedly, through misconfiguration or a DoS attack, even in a loop between gateways. The client SHOULD limit the number of redirects within a short period for one IKEv2 SA setup. The defaults are 5 for MAX_REDIRECTS and 300 seconds for REDIRECT_LOOP_DETECT_PERIOD.

For Mobile IPv6, the mechanism lets a home agent redirect a mobile node before any binding state exists, unlike the Home Agent Switch mechanism, which only works after the binding cache has been created. The mobile node MAY treat an address received in IKE_SA_INIT like other unauthenticated discovery information, and authenticated home agent information MUST NOT be updated from it. Gateway-initiated INFORMATIONAL redirects MUST NOT update any Mobile IPv6 state.

The mechanism is mainly for client-gateway use but works between any two IKEv2 peers. It is asymmetric: only the original responder can redirect the original initiator.
sections.plainLanguage: If you keep being sent from door to door, you give up after a few tries instead of walking in circles forever.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
An on-path eavesdropper can send a redirect to a client after seeing its IKE_SA_INIT message. It could already drop the request, but it could also redirect many clients to a victim, which would be flooded with IKE_SA_INIT requests. The RFC considers this rare, since it needs many clients starting at nearly the same time, such as after a gateway is shut down for maintenance. REDIRECTED_FROM is meant to discourage a rogue gateway from redirecting many clients to one target, but it does not prevent the attack.

The redirect mechanism MUST NOT update client state apart from the gateway information. Redirecting based on unauthenticated client identities might leak user information to an active attacker, so it should be avoided and done only after the client has authenticated itself.
sections.plainLanguage: A trickster standing in the hallway could point lots of visitors at one innocent shop. The rules make that harder to do but cannot stop it completely.
